lessons: Match the auth signature only on the CLI's own failure channel: claude's result-event error text (parsed.failure) plus stderr, and codex's error/turn.failed message plus stderr. Never search the whole stdout transcript, because tool output in it can contain the phrase.

Give each adapter a distinct signature that matches its real expired-login text. Claude prints e.g. 'Please run /login' or an OAuth-expired message; codex prints a 401/refresh or login failure. Don't share one generic 'Not logged in'. Use a case-sensitive literal match.
Add a test where the signature appears only in assistant/tool content inside a failing stream while the result and stderr lack it, and assert failure_class is None.
Everything else passed checks and review: the Driver mapping, the tests, the shakeout member and the registry entry. Keep them, and only update the fixture strings to the new per-CLI signatures.
reason: Review snag: the auth signature is matched across the whole stdout transcript. That is a fixable oversight and the review finding already names the fix.
